title: Distribution and economic value of rock types in Ethiopia
competency: Describe where the different rock types are found in Ethiopia and their economic value.

keywords.def: Where something is found across an area, such as which rocks cover which parts of Ethiopia.
Fuels found in sedimentary rocks: coal, petroleum and natural gas.
Sodium chloride from sedimentary rock, used in cooking.
Rock formed when magma or lava cools and hardens. From the Latin ignis, fire.
Rock formed in layers from settled sediments. Holds fossils, coal, oil and gas.
Rock formed when heat and pressure change an existing rock. Example: marble.

en.text: All three rock types are found in Ethiopia. Igneous rocks cover large areas in the centre of the country. Eastern Ethiopia is mainly covered by sedimentary rocks. Metamorphic rocks are found along the northern, western and southern edges.

en.text: Rocks are useful to people. Coal from sedimentary rock is fuel for industry. Granite and sandstone are quarried for roads, bridges and buildings. Marble decorates floors and walls. Rock salt is used in cooking. Soils form when rocks break down. Metals like gold and copper are linked with metamorphic rocks.

screens.title: Rocks at home and school
screens.text: Many everyday things come from rocks.
screens.ask: Tap at least three things. Guess which rock type each comes from.
items: Rock salt comes from sedimentary rock.
Chalk is a writing material linked with sedimentary rock.
Gold is linked with metamorphic rock.
Marble is metamorphic rock, polished for decoration.
Basalt and granite are igneous building stone.
Copper is linked with metamorphic rock.

screens.title: B. Economic importance of rocks in Ethiopia
paras: Rocks have many uses that make them important to people.
1. Fuel: sedimentary rocks such as coal are a source of fuel for industry.
2. Construction: granite and sandstone are quarried for roads, bridges and buildings. Marble is polished to decorate floors and walls.
3. Food: rock salt (sodium chloride) from sedimentary rock is used in cooking.
4. Soil: soils form when rocks slowly break down.

screens.title: Table 1.3 Rocks, minerals and uses
paras: Each rock type is linked with different minerals and uses.
table: Metals: gold, nickel, copper, uranium, iron, platinum, lead; also diamond
Jewellery and decoration, construction, electrical wire, industrial machinery
Mineral fuels: coal, petroleum, natural gas; also limestone and gypsum

screens.title: Looking for petroleum
screens.text: A company wants to search for petroleum in Ethiopia.
screens.ask: Based on this lesson, where should it look first?
screens.why: Petroleum is found in sedimentary rock, which covers mainly eastern Ethiopia.
screens.clue: Which rock type holds petroleum? Where is that rock type found?
screens.worked: Table 1.3: petroleum is a mineral fuel in sedimentary rock. Part A: eastern Ethiopia is mainly sedimentary. So look in the east.

screens.title: Coal

screens.why: Coal is a mineral fuel found in sedimentary rock.
screens.clue: Which rock type forms in layers and stores energy resources?

screens.title: Soil

screens.why: Soil formation is one of the important values of rocks.

items.why: Addis Ababa is in the centre, which is mostly igneous.

screens.title: How each rock forms
screens.text: Rocks are grouped by how they form (Lesson 1.4).
steps: Igneous: magma or lava cools and hardens. Example: basalt, granite.
Sedimentary: sediments settle in layers. Example: limestone, coal.
Metamorphic: heat and pressure change an existing rock. Example: marble.

screens.title: Your turn
screens.text: Coal formed from layers of old plants. What type of rock is it?
screens.why: It formed from settled layers, so it is sedimentary.
screens.clue: Did it cool, settle or change?
